completedPhaseClaims.provenanceNote: GATE G022 CHECK 6B STILL REFUSES THIS CLAIM, and that refusal is CORRECT rather than a defect in this record. workflows.yaml registers the owner of the 'implement' phase as bubbles.implement; the only agent this packet records as having executed it is bubbles.goal, under provenanceMode 'direct'. Check 6B accepts exactly two shapes: Pass 1 wants an executionHistory entry whose agent is the registered owner (or the bubbles.bug delegation shortcut) with provenanceMode '' or 'specialist'; Pass 2 wants provenanceMode 'parent-expanded' plus an expansionReason naming a capability that was missing. Neither is available truthfully. Renaming the agent to bubbles.implement would fabricate an agent that never ran, which is the impersonation this gate exists to catch. Re-labelling the mode 'parent-expanded' would require asserting that runSubagent or a nested runtime was unavailable, and nothing in this packet records that -- it records the opposite, an authorised direct run (execution.executionModel is 'direct-authorized-runner'). The claim is therefore left standing with its real provenance and the gate is left red.

notes: Pre-existing defect, not introduced by this session's commits.

A1 (audit): scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh passes `-p 1`; no contending file calls t.Parallel(); the go/python lanes are sequential docker runs. The two packages never run concurrently, so the documented interleaving was unreachable during the original red.
The landed lock is DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH: it makes exclusion a property of the namespace rather than of a flag in a shell script, and covers a future `-p >1` or a shared-DB cross-lane run.

F4 is the primary remaining hypothesis: internal/assistant/selfknowledge/ingestor.go deletes every smackerel_self row whose content_hash is absent from the corpus, which is every row these tests insert. It runs at core boot, and the core container is not serialised by -p 1.
The production stale sweep itself is designed behaviour and is unchanged.
